rows.currentScript: Turn to “hour”, after the gap. Its h is silent, so a vowel sound comes first. That sound takes “an”, so “an hour” fits. The others leave “a hour” or “spent hour”.
rows.whyRewrite: 'The others leave "a hour" or "spent hour".' does not describe the option 'the' ('spent the hour'), which is grammatical and needs its own reason (no particular hour has been named). A wrong option is left described wrongly. The silent-h reasoning for 'an' is correct.

rows.currentScript: Go straight to “said Dev”, above the gap. That is simple past, like “walked” and “stood”. The gap keeps step, so “replied” fits. The others move the talk into today.
rows.whyRewrite: Not on the screen: 'Go straight to "said Dev", above the gap.' This stem is only '"I am not fixing the whole school," Maya ___. "I am fixing one corridor." Dev shrugged.' 'said Dev' and 'stood' are not shown ('walked' is in another item). Anchor on 'Dev shrugged' instead; key 'replied' is correct.

rows.currentScript: Start at “not rubbish”, just after the gap. Only one choice stretches into “they are”. They are not rubbish, so “They’re” fits. “Their” and “theirs” show owning, “there” points at a place.
rows.whyRewrite: Comma splice in child-facing SPaG text: '"Their" and "theirs" show owning, "there" points at a place.' joins two sentences with a comma (the very fault PU-04 teaches). Split with a full stop or add 'and'. Key 'They're' correct.

rows.currentScript: Turn to the half before the gap. “If we painted” shows no lid is painted. An if like that takes “would”, so “would know” fits. The others make it real, or look back.
rows.whyRewrite: 'The others make it real, or look back.' does not describe 'would be knowing' ('will know' makes it real, 'would have known' looks back; 'would be knowing' does neither, it is simply not used with 'know'). A wrong option described wrongly. Key 'would know' and the if-reasoning are correct.

rows.currentScript: Read either side of the gap. The joining word stands for “the girl”, who does the worrying. A person doing the action takes “who”. The line offers no thing, nothing owned, nothing done to her.
rows.whyRewrite: 'The joining word stands for "the girl", who does the worrying.' contradicts the line: she 'never worried'. Say she is the one the verb is about (e.g. 'who never worried'). Key 'who' and the which/whose/whom contrasts are correct.

rows.currentScript: Look after the gap, at “crowd”. The gap tells us what the crowd was like. The -ing form does that job: the cheering crowd. The others have the crowd doing, or being cheered.
rows.whyRewrite: First person: 'The gap tells us what the crowd was like.' Also 'The others have the crowd doing, or being cheered.' misdescribes 'cheer' and 'cheers', which do not have the crowd doing anything in 'The ___ crowd'. Key 'cheering' correct.

rows.currentScript: Turn to the sentence before the gap. Mrs Lawson wrote his time on “a board”. A board we have met takes “the”. The others start a new board, or leave none.
rows.whyRewrite: First person: 'A board we have met takes "the".' Reword without 'we' (e.g. 'A board already mentioned takes "the".'). Key 'the' and the reasoning are correct.

rows.currentScript: Look at the fourth part, at “excellant”. We write “excellence” with -ence, and -ence goes with -ent. So an e goes where the a is, and the fourth part has the mistake. The three earlier parts hold.
rows.whyRewrite: First person: 'We write "excellence" with -ence, and -ence goes with -ent.' Reword without 'we'. The spelling claim (excellent, -ent with -ence) is correct and the key is right.

rows.currentScript: Start at the first part, at the day name. Say it slowly: Wed-nes-day. That middle d is missing from “Wenesday”. “Knights”, “wrote” and “hall” hold.
rows.whyRewrite: 'That middle d is missing from "Wenesday".' is inaccurate: the missing d is the third letter, at the end of 'Wed', not a middle d (the d's in Wednesday are letters 3 and 7 of 9). Say 'The d at the end of Wed is missing.' Key correct.

rows.currentScript: Go straight to the third part, at “definitely”. It is “de” plus “finite”, so the middle letter is an i. “Wednesday” and “choir” keep their odd letters. “Separately” keeps the a of “separate”, and “hall” is the room. Every part holds, so nothing needs changing.
rows.whyRewrite: 'so the middle letter is an i' is inaccurate: the middle of 'definitely' (10 letters) is n-i, and the letter a child gets wrong is the one after the n. Say which letter (e.g. 'the letter after the n is an i'). Key No mistake and all other spellings correct.
